To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ribosome-free Trigger Factor (TF) stably associates with a large repertoire of substrate proteins, including the ribosomal protein S6, that TF promotes protein folding, and that the atomic-level structure of a TF:S6 complex provides a molecular basis of substrate binding and a possible mechanism for chaperone function.

ribosome-free trigger factor (TF) rescues from misfolded state a large repertoire of cytosolic proteins in Escherichia coli, and we determined the atomic structure of a physiological TF:ribosomal protein S7 (S7) complex.

the molecular chaperone trigger factor (TF) recognizes a large repertoire of substrate proteins, including the ribosomal protein S-7, and promotes their folding in vitro, and that TF recognizes its substrates via a promiscuous interaction that involves a hydrophobic surface of the substrate protein and the hydrophobic cavity of TF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the trigger factor (TF) chaperone.
the molecular mechanism of protein folding.
the structure and function of molecular chaperones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TF has a much broader substrate repertoire than previously appreciated.
the chaperone TF has a much wider range of activities than previously thought.
TF is not a promiscuous molecular chaperone but rather a highly promiscuous molecular folding catalyst.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that TF has a much broader role in protein biogenesis than previously appreciated.
TF is an important cytosolic chaperone with a broad substrate repertoire that includes proteins with complex quaternary structures.
TF has a broad substrate specificity and is a promiscuous molecular chaperone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TF is a promiscuous protein folding and assembly chaperone.
a single molecular chaperone, TF, can bind to many different proteins and can promote their folding and assembly in the cytosolic environment.
TF is not a ribosome-specific chaperone, but a general protein folding chaperone.
